# RDF Modeling for Graphmind

When helping users build or manage knowledge graphs stored as RDF data, follow these modeling patterns and conventions.

## Choosing Vocabularies

Prefer established vocabularies over inventing custom predicates. Mixing vocabularies in a single graph is normal and encouraged.

### Common vocabularies

| Prefix | Namespace | Use for |
|--------|-----------|---------|
| `foaf:` | `http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/` | People, social connections, online accounts |
| `schema:` | `http://schema.org/` | General-purpose: events, organizations, products, places |
| `dcterms:` | `http://purl.org/dc/terms/` | Metadata: title, creator, date, description, subject |
| `skos:` | `http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#` | Taxonomies, concept schemes, labels |
| `rdfs:` | `http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#` | Labels, comments, class/property hierarchies |
| `xsd:` | `http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#` | Datatypes: string, integer, date, boolean |

### When to create custom predicates

Only create custom predicates when no existing vocabulary covers the concept. Use a project-specific namespace:

```turtle
@prefix rdf:     <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#> .
@prefix rdfs:    <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#> .
@prefix project: <http://ns.project.example/ns/project#> .

project:dependsOn   a rdf:Property ;
    rdfs:label "depends on"@en ;
    rdfs:comment "Indicates a dependency between project components"@en .
```

## Turtle File Structure

### Standard file layout

```turtle
# -- Prefixes --
@prefix rdf:     <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#> .
@prefix rdfs:    <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#> .
@prefix dcterms: <http://purl.org/dc/terms/> .
@prefix xsd:     <http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#> .
@prefix foaf:    <http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/> .
@prefix :        <http://ns.project.example/data/> .

# -- Schema (classes and properties) --
:Project a rdfs:Class ;
    rdfs:label "Project"@en .

# -- Data (instances) --
:my-project a :Project ;
    rdfs:label "My Project"@en ;
    dcterms:created "2024-01-15"^^xsd:date .
```

### Naming conventions

- **URIs for resources**: Use kebab-case slugs: `http://ns.project.example/data/my-resource`
- **Predicates**: Use camelCase: `schema:dateCreated`, `foaf:firstName`
- **Classes**: Use PascalCase: `foaf:Person`, `schema:Organization`
- **Blank nodes**: Avoid when possible. Use them only for truly anonymous resources (e.g., an address embedded in a person record)

## Modeling Patterns

### Typing resources

Always give resources an `rdf:type` (shorthand `a`):

```turtle
@prefix foaf: <http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/> .
@prefix :     <http://ns.project.example/data/> .

:alice a foaf:Person ;
    foaf:name "Alice" .
```

### Linking resources

Use object properties to connect resources:

```turtle
@prefix foaf:   <http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/> .
@prefix schema: <http://schema.org/> .
@prefix :       <http://ns.project.example/data/> .

:alice foaf:knows :bob .
:alice schema:worksFor :acme-corp .
```

### Literal values with datatypes

```turtle
@prefix schema:  <http://schema.org/> .
@prefix dcterms: <http://purl.org/dc/terms/> .
@prefix xsd:     <http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#> .
@prefix :        <http://ns.project.example/data/> .

:event schema:startDate "2024-06-15"^^xsd:date .
:product schema:price "29.99"^^xsd:decimal .
:document dcterms:title "Knowledge Graph Design"@en .
```

### Collections and ordering

For ordered lists, use `rdf:first`/`rdf:rest` or schema.org's `ItemList`:

```turtle
@prefix schema: <http://schema.org/> .
@prefix :       <http://ns.project.example/data/> .

:playlist a schema:ItemList ;
    schema:itemListElement [
        a schema:ListItem ;
        schema:position 1 ;
        schema:item :song-a
    ] , [
        a schema:ListItem ;
        schema:position 2 ;
        schema:item :song-b
    ] .
```

### Reification (statements about statements)

When you need to annotate a fact (e.g., "Alice knows Bob since 2020"), use named graphs or RDF-star:

```turtle
@prefix foaf:    <http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/> .
@prefix dcterms: <http://purl.org/dc/terms/> .
@prefix xsd:     <http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#> .
@prefix :        <http://ns.project.example/data/> .

# RDF-star syntax (if supported)
<<:alice foaf:knows :bob>> dcterms:created "2020-01-01"^^xsd:date .
```

## File Organization

### Recommended project structure

```
vocab/
  people.ttl      # Person-related classes and properties
  projects.ttl    # Project-related classes and properties
knowledge/
  people.ttl      # Person instances and data
  projects.ttl    # Project instances and data
```

### Splitting by concern

- Keep schema (TBox) separate from data (ABox)
- Group related resources in the same file
- Use consistent prefixes across all files in a project

## Validation Checklist

Before querying a newly created knowledge graph, verify:

1. Every resource has an `rdf:type`
2. Every predicate is either from a known vocabulary or defined in the schema file
3. Literal datatypes match the property's expected range (dates as `xsd:date`, numbers as `xsd:integer` or `xsd:decimal`)
4. URIs are well-formed and use consistent namespaces
5. Language tags are present on human-readable strings (`"label"@en`)

# SPARQL Query Patterns for Graphmind

When helping users query knowledge graphs with the `sparql_query` tool, follow these patterns and best practices. Use `sparql_query` for local Turtle files, SPARQL endpoints, Triple Pattern Fragment servers, Solid pods, or any URL serving RDF data.

## Query Patterns

### SELECT -- Retrieve specific values

```sparql
SELECT ?subject ?predicate ?object
WHERE {
  ?subject ?predicate ?object .
}
LIMIT 10
```

Use SELECT when the user wants tabular data or specific property values.

### CONSTRUCT -- Generate RDF triples

```sparql
CONSTRUCT {
  ?person a <http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/Person> ;
    <http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/name> ?name .
}
WHERE {
  ?person a <http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/Person> ;
    <http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/name> ?name .
}
```

Use CONSTRUCT when the user wants to extract or reshape RDF data. Output defaults to Turtle format.

### ASK -- Boolean check

```sparql
ASK {
  <http://data.project.example/resource> a <http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/Person> .
}
```

Use ASK when the user wants to verify whether a fact exists in the graph.

### DESCRIBE -- Get everything about a resource

```sparql
DESCRIBE <http://data.project.example/resource>
```

Use DESCRIBE when the user wants all known triples about a specific resource.

## Filtering and Aggregation

### FILTER with string matching

```sparql
SELECT ?label WHERE {
  ?s rdfs:label ?label .
  FILTER(CONTAINS(LCASE(?label), "search term"))
}
```

### GROUP BY with aggregation

```sparql
SELECT ?type (COUNT(?instance) AS ?count)
WHERE {
  ?instance a ?type .
}
GROUP BY ?type
ORDER BY DESC(?count)
LIMIT 10
```

### OPTIONAL for nullable properties

```sparql
SELECT ?name ?email WHERE {
  ?person foaf:name ?name .
  OPTIONAL { ?person foaf:mbox ?email . }
}
```

## Source Handling

### Local files

Pass relative paths from the project root. The tool resolves them and converts to file:// URLs internally. Supported formats: Turtle (.ttl), N-Triples (.nt), JSON-LD (.jsonld), RDF/XML (.rdf).

```json
{
  "sources": ["knowledge/data.ttl", "knowledge/schema.ttl"]
}
```

### Multiple sources

The `sparql_query` tool can query across multiple sources simultaneously. Use this when the user's data is spread across multiple files or endpoints.

### Output formats

- Prefer `application/json` (default) for SELECT queries -- easiest for the agent to parse
- Prefer `text/turtle` (default) for CONSTRUCT -- standard RDF serialization
- Offer `text/csv` when the user wants to save results to a file

## Error Recovery

- **Timeout**: Suggest simplifying the query (fewer triple patterns, lower LIMIT) or increasing `httpTimeout`
- **Syntax errors**: Check for missing dots at end of triple patterns, unmatched braces, incorrect prefix usage
- **No results**: Check if properties exist for the entity, try broadening the query
- **File not found**: Verify the file path is relative to the project root and the file exists

# Wikidata Knowledge Skill

Use the `wikidata_query` tool to answer factual questions about the real world. Wikidata is the world's largest open knowledge base, containing structured data about people, places, events, organizations, scientific concepts, and much more.

## Query Construction

### Always include the label service

Every query should include the label service to get human-readable names instead of opaque IDs:

```sparql
SELECT ?itemLabel ?value WHERE {
  ?item wdt:P31 wd:Q5 .
  ?item wdt:P569 ?value .
  SERVICE wikibase:label { bd:serviceParam wikibase:language "en". }
}
```

Variables ending in `Label` (like `?itemLabel`) are automatically populated by the label service.

### Finding entity IDs

When the user mentions a real-world entity, you need its Wikidata ID. Common patterns:

- People: `wdt:P31 wd:Q5` (instance of human)
- Countries: `wdt:P31 wd:Q6256` (instance of country)
- Cities: `wdt:P31 wd:Q515` (instance of city)
- Companies: `wdt:P31 wd:Q4830453` (instance of business enterprise)
- Films: `wdt:P31 wd:Q11424` (instance of film)
- Universities: `wdt:P31 wd:Q3918` (instance of university)
- Programming languages: `wdt:P31 wd:Q9143` (instance of programming language)

For specific entities, use their Q-ID directly: `wd:Q42` (Douglas Adams), `wd:Q90` (Paris), `wd:Q2` (Earth).

### Common properties

- `wdt:P31` -- instance of (what type of thing is this?)
- `wdt:P279` -- subclass of
- `wdt:P17` -- country
- `wdt:P569` -- date of birth
- `wdt:P570` -- date of death
- `wdt:P106` -- occupation
- `wdt:P27` -- country of citizenship
- `wdt:P625` -- coordinate location
- `wdt:P571` -- inception / date founded
- `wdt:P112` -- founded by
- `wdt:P1082` -- population
- `wdt:P2044` -- elevation above sea level
- `wdt:P57` -- director (film)
- `wdt:P161` -- cast member
- `wdt:P166` -- award received
- `wdt:P69` -- educated at
- `wdt:P108` -- employer
- `wdt:P47` -- shares border with
- `wdt:P36` -- capital
- `wdt:P37` -- official language

## Query Examples

### Simple lookup

"When was Albert Einstein born?"

```sparql
SELECT ?birthDate WHERE {
  wd:Q937 wdt:P569 ?birthDate .
}
```

### List with labels

"What are the official languages of Switzerland?"

```sparql
SELECT ?languageLabel WHERE {
  wd:Q39 wdt:P37 ?language .
  SERVICE wikibase:label { bd:serviceParam wikibase:language "en". }
}
```

### Aggregation

"Which countries have the highest population?"

```sparql
SELECT ?countryLabel ?population WHERE {
  ?country wdt:P31 wd:Q6256 .
  ?country wdt:P1082 ?population .
  SERVICE wikibase:label { bd:serviceParam wikibase:language "en". }
}
ORDER BY DESC(?population)
LIMIT 10
```

### Filtering by date range

"Which Nobel Prize winners were born after 1950?"

```sparql
SELECT ?personLabel ?birthDate ?prizeLabel WHERE {
  ?person wdt:P166 ?prize .
  ?prize wdt:P31/wdt:P279* wd:Q7191 .
  ?person wdt:P569 ?birthDate .
  FILTER(?birthDate > "1950-01-01"^^xsd:dateTime)
  SERVICE wikibase:label { bd:serviceParam wikibase:language "en". }
}
ORDER BY ?birthDate
LIMIT 20
```

### Relationships between entities

"Which cities are capitals of EU member states?"

```sparql
SELECT ?countryLabel ?capitalLabel WHERE {
  ?country wdt:P463 wd:Q458 .
  ?country wdt:P36 ?capital .
  SERVICE wikibase:label { bd:serviceParam wikibase:language "en". }
}
ORDER BY ?countryLabel
```

## Tips

- Start with simple queries and add complexity. If a query returns no results, simplify it.
- Use `LIMIT` to keep results manageable (start with 10-20).
- For complex queries, increase `httpTimeout` beyond the default 30 seconds.
- When unsure of an entity's Q-ID, search by label:
  ```sparql
  SELECT ?item ?itemLabel WHERE {
    ?item rdfs:label "Berlin"@en .
    SERVICE wikibase:label { bd:serviceParam wikibase:language "en". }
  }
  LIMIT 5
  ```
- Use `OPTIONAL` for properties that might not exist for all results.
- The `wikidata_query` tool auto-injects common prefixes (wd:, wdt:, p:, ps:, pq:, wikibase:, bd:, rdfs:), so you do not need to declare them.

# graphmind

Knowledge graphs as a long-term memory for your AI assistants

## Installation

### From npm

Add the plugin and built-in skills to your OpenCode configuration:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugin": ["graphmind"],
  "skills": {
    "paths": ["~/.cache/opencode/node_modules/graphmind/skill"]
  }
}
```

OpenCode will automatically install the plugin on startup. See the [Skills](#skills) section for available skills and alternative path configurations.

## Features

### Wikidata Query Tool

Query Wikidata for factual information about the world using the `wikidata_query` tool. This tool is optimized for querying the Wikidata knowledge base, which contains structured data about people, places, events, concepts, and more.

**Key Features:**

- Automatic Wikidata prefix injection (wd:, wdt:, p:, ps:, pq:, etc.)
- Optimized default timeout for Wikidata queries (30 seconds)
- Helpful error messages with guidance for common issues
- Support for Wikidata-specific features like the label service

**Use Cases:**

- Historical facts and events
- Geographical data and locations
- Information about people and organizations
- Scientific concepts and classifications
- Cultural and general world knowledge

### SPARQL Query Tool

Execute SPARQL queries over RDF data sources using the `sparql_query` tool. This tool uses Comunica under the hood to provide flexible querying capabilities.

**Supported Query Types:**

- `SELECT` - Retrieve bindings for variables
- `CONSTRUCT` - Generate RDF triples
- `DESCRIBE` - Retrieve RDF descriptions
- `ASK` - Boolean queries

**Supported Data Sources:**

- SPARQL endpoints (e.g., DBpedia, Wikidata)
- Triple Pattern Fragments (TPF) servers
- RDF files (Turtle, N-Triples, JSON-LD, etc.)
- Solid pods
- Any URL serving RDF data

## Usage Examples

### Wikidata Queries

#### Find Information About a Person

```
Who is Douglas Adams and when was he born?
```

OpenCode will construct a Wikidata query like:

```json
{
  "query": "SELECT ?personLabel ?birthDate WHERE { wd:Q42 wdt:P569 ?birthDate. SERVICE wikibase:label { bd:serviceParam wikibase:language 'en'. } }"
}
```

#### Find Countries by Population

```
What are the 10 most populous countries in the world?
```

#### Historical Events

```
What major events happened in 1969?
```

The tool automatically adds all necessary Wikidata prefixes, so you can focus on writing the query logic.

### Basic SELECT Query

Query DBpedia for the first 10 triples:

```
Can you query DBpedia for the first 10 triples?
```

OpenCode will use the tool with parameters like:

```json
{
  "query": "SELECT * WHERE { ?s ?p ?o } LIMIT 10",
  "sources": ["https://fragments.dbpedia.org/2016-04/en"]
}
```

### Query Multiple Sources

Query across multiple RDF sources simultaneously:

```
Query DBpedia and Wikidata for entities related to "artificial intelligence"
```

### CONSTRUCT Query

Generate RDF triples:

```
Use a CONSTRUCT query to get book information from DBpedia
```

### Custom Output Format

Request specific output formats:

```json
{
  "query": "SELECT * WHERE { ?s ?p ?o } LIMIT 10",
  "sources": ["https://fragments.dbpedia.org/2016-04/en"],
  "outputFormat": "text/csv"
}
```

**Available Output Formats:**

- `application/json` (default for SELECT)
- `application/sparql-results+json`
- `application/sparql-results+xml`
- `text/csv`
- `text/tab-separated-values`
- `text/turtle` (default for CONSTRUCT)
- `application/trig`
- `application/n-triples`
- `application/n-quads`
- `application/ld+json`

### Advanced Options

```json
{
  "query": "SELECT * WHERE { ?s ?p ?o } LIMIT 10",
  "sources": ["https://fragments.dbpedia.org/2016-04/en"],
  "baseIRI": "http://example.org/",
  "lenient": true,
  "httpTimeout": 30000,
  "logLevel": "debug"
}
```

## Tool Parameters

### `wikidata_query`

| Parameter      | Type   | Required | Description                                              |
| -------------- | ------ | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `query`        | string | Yes      | SPARQL query for Wikidata (prefixes added automatically) |
| `outputFormat` | string | No       | Output format: json, csv, tsv, xml (default: json)       |
| `httpTimeout`  | number | No       | HTTP timeout in milliseconds (default: 30000)            |
| `logLevel`     | string | No       | Log level: error, warn, info, or debug                   |

**Note:** The tool automatically adds common Wikidata prefixes (wd:, wdt:, p:, ps:, pq:, wikibase:, bd:, rdfs:) if they're not already in your query.

### `sparql_query`

| Parameter      | Type     | Required | Description                             |
| -------------- | -------- | -------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `query`        | string   | Yes      | The SPARQL query string to execute      |
| `sources`      | string[] | Yes      | One or more URLs to query over          |
| `outputFormat` | string   | No       | Output format for results               |
| `baseIRI`      | string   | No       | Base IRI for the query                  |
| `lenient`      | boolean  | No       | If true, log errors instead of throwing |
| `httpTimeout`  | number   | No       | HTTP request timeout in milliseconds    |
| `logLevel`     | string   | No       | Log level: error, warn, info, or debug  |

## Skills

Graphmind ships domain-specific skills that give your AI agent knowledge about SPARQL query patterns and RDF modeling conventions. Skills are instruction files that improve how agents use the plugin's tools.

### Available Skills

| Skill | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `graphmind-wikidata` | Answer real-world factual questions by querying Wikidata, the world's largest open knowledge base |
| `graphmind-sparql-patterns` | Common SPARQL query patterns for querying RDF knowledge graphs with Graphmind |
| `graphmind-rdf-modeling` | RDF modeling patterns and ontology conventions for knowledge graph construction |

### Enabling Skills

Add the skills path to your `opencode.json`:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugin": ["graphmind"],
  "skills": {
    "paths": ["node_modules/graphmind/skills"]
  }
}
```

If OpenCode installed the plugin to its cache directory, use the cache path instead:

```json
{
  "skills": {
    "paths": ["~/.cache/opencode/node_modules/graphmind/skills"]
  }
}
```

For local plugin installations, point to the local path:

```json
{
  "skills": {
    "paths": [".opencode/plugins/graphmind/skills"]
  }
}
```

## Requirements

- Node.js >= 18.0.0
- The plugin automatically installs Comunica dependencies
